children: GOOG Q3 revenue $127.6B (+25%); Google Cloud $30.7B (+~103%); Search ads +12%, YouTube +9%. Negative free cash flow ~$9.07B. Diluted/non-GAAP EPS $2.12–$2.67. CapEx ~$51.4B; no buybacks YTD.
GOOG fell about 12.6% intraday after earnings, wiping roughly $500B from market value. Traders noted rising investment costs and a weaker search-ad outlook; analysts said they will revise estimates.
GOOG posted first negative free cash flow in 22 years: about -$9.07B for the quarter, driven by higher capex for AI, data centers and cloud, a $5.2B EU fine payment, and a SpaceX investment loss.
Alphabet Class C (GOOG) plans about $300B in spending next year and reported negative free cash flow, data traders use to gauge cash generation and capital allocation.
GOOG faces trader focus on AI spending vs. cash flow: whether near-term AI investments will outpace operating cash generation and impact cash-burn dynamics.
Citigroup cut GOOG target to $375 from $447; Wells Fargo trimmed target to $371 from $417. Citi's $375 and Wells' $371 imply notable upside versus recent closes near $278–$282.
GOOG bought $131.953B in property and equipment in nine months, outpacing operating cash flow of $127.149B by $4.804B; timing of deliveries, customer usage and payments affect cash conversion.
GOOG: Q/Q Cloud revenue +103% to $30.7B; Gemini AI cited as a growth driver. Analysts cut price targets but kept mixed to neutral ratings; shares slid post-earnings.
GOOG reported quarterly results showing slower Google revenue growth, citing shifts in user behavior and AI-driven search changes, noting a softer near-term path for core Google Services.
GOOG five-year CDS widened to 85 bps from 61 bps, a 24-bp increase, raising the market cost to insure Alphabet’s five-year debt against default.
